 For the Informant: Mr. Shashank Kumar

The petitioners apprehending their arrest in connection with the case
registered under Sections 376/313/323/341/498A/420/494/34 Ipc, Sections 3/4 of Dowry
Prohibition Act and Section 6 of Pocso Act have prayed for grant of anticipatory bail.
2. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the petitioners have been falsely implicated in this case and have not committed any offence as alleged in the F.I.R.
The petitioner No.1 is the father-in-law, the petitioner No.2 is the mother-in-law and the petitioner No.3 is their close relative.
It is further submitted that the present FIR has been lodged only due to the reason that the informant/victim wanted to live separately with her husband, which was objected by the petitioners.
However, after intervention of the family members, friends and well wishers, the informant/victim has settled the dispute with the accused persons including the petitioners.

A joint compromise petition to that effect was also filed at the time of consideration of A.B.P. No. 17/2024 by learned Additional Sessions Judge-I-cum-Special Judge (POCSO), Lohardaga and a copy of the same has been annexed as Annexure-2 to the present anticipatory bail application.
Under the said circumstance, the petitioners may be given the privilege of anticipatory bail.

Learned counsel for the informant/victim refers to the counter affidavit dated 03.09.2024 filed on behalf of the informant/victim and submits that after intervention of some mutual friends of both the families as well as respectable members of the society, the dispute between the accused persons including the petitioners and the informant/victim has amicably been settled.
The informant/victim is willing to return to her matrimonial home and the petitioners have agreed to keep her with full dignity.
4. Learned counsel for the informant/victim, on instruction, submits that the informant/victim is presently staying with her husband, namely, Sikandar Sahu in her matrimonial home.

5. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and considering that the accused persons including the petitioners and the informant have amicably settled the dispute and the said fact has been accepted by the informant/victim in her counter affidavit dated 03.09.2024, I am inclined to enlarge the petitioners on anticipatory bail.
Accordingly, the above named petitioners are directed to surrender before the concerned Court below within a period of three weeks.

If they surrender before the Court below within the aforesaid period, they shall be released on bail on furnishing bail-bond of Rs.20,000/- (twenty thousand only) each with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Additional Sessions Judge-I-cum-Special Judge, Lohardaga in connection with Lohardaga Mahila P.S. Case No. 36/2023, subject to the conditions as laid down under Section 438(2) Cr.P.C.
